issues.legal_issue: A person who uses force to repel an imminent attack is entitled to complete acquittal when the circumstances establish the right of private defence.
material_facts: The prosecution party attacked the accused and his brothers with cutting weapons and sticks, causing the accused head injuries and causing one brother severe injuries, including fractures.
The accused was not armed when the occurrence began and did not use his gun while the initial attack was taking place.

After the severely injured brother was left outside the house, the accused and another brother entered the house, while the prosecution party continued pelting bricks and stones and tried to enter by scaling the wall.
The prosecution party threatened to kill the accused and his brother and claimed that they had already killed the brother who was lying outside.
The accused first fired shots in the air to frighten the crowd and fired at it only when it continued toward the house; the resulting injuries to the witnesses were simple.
The accused appealed his convictions, and the Court considered the appeal on the plea of private defence.
issues.conclusion: The accused was entitled to complete acquittal on the plea of private defence; the convictions and sentences were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The right of private defence of the person permits a complete acquittal where the circumstances give rise to a reasonable apprehension of imminent danger and the force used is in response to that danger. The Court relied on the circumstances of the attack, the threats, the attempted entry into the house and the accused's resort to firing only after warning shots proved ineffective. No particular statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the judgment for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and armed_attack_caused_serious_injuries and attackers_pursued_defenders_to_shelter and attackers_threatened_imminent_killing and defender_warned_before_firing and defender_fired_only_after_threat_persisted

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: A person convicted of an offence appealed against the conviction.
predicates.armed_attack_caused_serious_injuries: An attacking group used weapons against the defender or the defender's companions and caused serious injuries.
predicates.attackers_pursued_defenders_to_shelter: After the initial attack, the attacking group pursued the defender or a companion toward a place of shelter and tried to enter it.
predicates.attackers_threatened_imminent_killing: The attacking group made threats indicating an imminent danger to the defender's or a companion's life.
predicates.defender_warned_before_firing: The defender first fired warning shots intended to frighten or deter the attacking group.
predicates.defender_fired_only_after_threat_persist: The defender fired at the attacking group only after it continued to present an imminent danger despite the warning.

issues.definition: When a convicted person appeals and the stated facts establish a serious attack, pursuit toward shelter, imminent threats, and firing only after an ineffective warning, the result is complete acquittal on private defence.

issues.legal_issue: A defender does not exceed the right of private defence by using force to repel an imminent threat after lesser measures fail to stop the attack.
material_facts: The prosecution party attacked the accused and his brothers with cutting weapons and sticks, causing the accused head injuries and causing one brother severe injuries, including fractures.
The accused did not use his gun during the initial attack and entered the house with another brother after the severely injured brother was left outside.
The prosecution party continued pelting bricks and stones, tried to enter the house by scaling the wall, and threatened to kill the accused and his brother.
The accused fired shots in the air first and fired at the crowd only when it continued toward the house; the witnesses' resulting injuries were simple.
The accused appealed his convictions, and the State argued that he had exceeded the right of private defence.
issues.conclusion: The accused did not exceed his right of private defence and was entitled to complete acquittal.
issues.legal_principle: Whether the right of private defence has been exceeded depends on the circumstances creating the apprehension of imminent danger and the defender's response to it. Here, the Court treated the initial attack, the severe injuries, the pursuit and threats, and the warning shots followed by firing only when the threat persisted as supporting the exercise of the right rather than its excess. No particular statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the judgment for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and defender_suffered_serious_injuries_in_initial_attack and attackers_continued_pursuit_and_threats and defender_used_warning_before_force and force_used_only_after_imminent_threat_persisted

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: A person convicted of an offence appealed against the conviction.
predicates.defender_suffered_serious_injuries_in_in: The defender suffered injuries during the initial attack by the opposing group.
predicates.attackers_continued_pursuit_and_threats: The opposing group pursued the defender or a companion and made threats of further serious harm.
predicates.defender_used_warning_before_force: The defender first used a warning intended to deter the opposing group before using force against it.
predicates.force_used_only_after_imminent_threat_pe: The defender used force against the opposing group only after it continued to pose an imminent danger.

issues.definition: When a convicted person appeals and the defender suffered injuries, faced continued pursuit and threats, warned the opposing group, and used force only after the imminent threat persisted, the result is that the right of private defence was not exceeded.
